_README: Broad-coverage evaluation cases, written 2026-09-27 after Phase 4, to cover what the 25 Phase 2 cases never touch: homicide, dowry death, kidnapping, robbery, intimidation, forgery, negligent death, extortion; facts written the way a lawyer's brief reads (names, FIR numbers, dates, procedural noise); and offence dates on both sides of 2024-07-01.
HELD OUT. Never tune retrieval, prompts or thresholds on these. Score once per method change; if anything is chosen BECAUSE of these results, write a new set.

Synthetic facts. Every section id in `relevant` was checked against the real ingested statute text (title and provision) before being assigned -- none from memory -- with scripts/check_fixture_ids.py, which fails on any id that is not an ingested section of the case's own code. The lists answer 'which sections do these facts disclose', a legal call made by Claude, NOT reviewed by a lawyer.
`arguable` names sections a court might reasonably add or substitute; a pipeline proposing one of those is not wrong.

Case 20 is a deliberate LIMITATION probe, not a gated case: a continuing course of cruelty straddling the transition. The router takes one offence date, so acts before 2024-07-01 (IPC 498A) and after (BNS 85) cannot both be charged from one run. Expected behaviour is to route on the date given and say nothing about the earlier acts -- which a report must warn about.

cases.query: After a quarrel over repayment of a loan, the accused went home, returned twenty minutes later with a kitchen knife and stabbed the deceased twice in the chest. The deceased died on the way to hospital. The post-mortem records that either wound was sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death.

Two neighbours argued about a drain. The argument turned into a sudden scuffle; the accused picked up a stick lying nearby and struck the deceased once on the head. There was no earlier enmity and no second blow. The deceased died two days later of a head injury.

The deceased married the accused in 2021. Her parents say the husband and his mother repeatedly demanded a car and two lakh rupees and beat her when her family could not pay. In February 2023, less than two years after the marriage, she died of burn injuries at the matrimonial home.

The accused, aged twenty-three, took the complainant's fifteen-year-old daughter from outside her school without her parents' knowledge or consent and kept her in a rented room in another town, telling her he would marry her.
At about 9 pm two men stopped the complainant on a lonely road, one held a knife to his neck and the other took his wallet, phone and gold chain. They ran off with the property.
After the complainant filed a police complaint against him, the accused phoned her three times and said he would kill her and her son if she did not withdraw it.

The accused prepared a sale deed of the complainant's plot bearing a forged signature of the complainant, got it registered, and then sold the plot to a third person for thirty lakh rupees, which he kept.
The accused was driving a loaded truck at high speed through a crowded market road while overtaking, lost control and ran over a pedestrian on the footpath, who died at the spot.

Brief: State v. Ramesh Kumar, FIR No. 412/2024, P.S. Sadar Bazar. Complainant Sh. Anil Gupta (proprietor, Gupta Jewellers) states that the accused Ramesh Kumar, employed with him as a salesman since March 2022, had access to the display counters. On 3 October 2024 stock verification disclosed a shortfall of four gold chains. CCTV footage dated 3.10.2024 shows the accused slipping two chains into his pocket at closing time. On his disclosure statement one chain was recovered from a pawn shop in Karol Bagh. Accused arrested on 5.10.2024; bail application pending before the Ld. CJM.
